correctness.rationale: For every length-two finite commutative chain ring, center reduction A↦(a-c,b) has Q scalar lifts; distinct primitive directions form P disjoint determinant-cliques, with QU matrix choices each. Nonprimitive vectors in m² form one determinant-clique and each has Q lifts; a single such vector forbids exactly q projective directions (the residue projective point fiber), leaving q² compatible ones. These cases exhaust all independent sets, giving the polynomial and highest coefficient. The proof checks endpoints q=2, k=0, k=P, and all finite prime powers. Standalone finite arithmetic and determinant enumeration for Z/4 and dual F2 verifies every coefficient; analogous structural checks for residue q=3; field-boundary checks. Finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The ordinary independence polynomial is an intrinsic full invariant of the commuting graph, refining the 2024 work on degrees and extremal parameters and the 2026 alpha classification. The first nilpotent chain-ring family includes both mixed-characteristic and equicharacteristic nonisomorphic rings, and its q-universal full coefficient distribution is not inferable from alpha alone. The explicit radical/projective-layer decomposition gives a reusable structural counting method and exact extremal multiplicities for a natural complete family; the question is not an arbitrary small instance or a known-table recomputation.
